clue.text: Come back to swot briefly, having got computerised facilities?

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to swot is to study hard for an exam

explanation.surface: A student returns to cramming for exams, now that the library has computers.
explanation.walkthrough: Swot is British for studying hard, and to revise is to study for an exam; the clipped word is followed by information technology's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to return to a place or topic, so it means come back to.

clue.text: A hundred abandoning creative activity? That's a large number

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so that letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a craft is a creative skill
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone giving up hobbies by the hundred is quitting a great many pastimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is informally a large number or quantity of them.

clue.text: Foreign noble's wickedness grabbing miss, one needing to escape

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the sin's word holds the other inside
the letter for one has to get out, so it is dropped from the word for miss

parts.note: to omit is to miss out

explanation.surface: A European aristocrat's depravity extends to seizing a young woman who must flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman but is the verb, to leave out.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicomte is a French nobleman, the equivalent of a British viscount.

clue.text: River trip led by head of school

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A headteacher heads a school outing along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Led by means the head's letter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is the name of several English rivers, notably in Dorset, Kent and Suffolk.

clue.text: Island jazz during which one awful noise is arising

indicators.note: during which places the following pieces within the music's word
in a down clue arising means going up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a din is an awful noise

explanation.surface: A Caribbean jazz session interrupted by a terrible racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Trad is the British name for traditional New Orleans-style jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of the Caribbean nation Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Result of the old man consumed by lust lacking energy ultimately?

definitions.text: Result of the old man consumed by lust lacking energy ultimately?

indicators.note: what is consumed ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes inside the other
the word for lust goes without its final letter, the E for energy

explanation.surface: An ageing man worn out by lust ends up hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: an exhausted, lustful old man ends in hopelessness, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair, utter hopelessness, is the plausible end state for a worn-out lecherous father.

clue.text: Bird losing tail caught up in river flood

indicators.note: something caught is trapped inside, so this goes within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top
losing its tail means the word's last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A tailless bird trapped in a flooded river.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or downpour of water.

clue.text: Excellent actress hanging loosely around part of the mansion?

indicators.note: things hanging loosely are slack and disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as I

explanation.surface: A star actress loafs about a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, top quality, supplies two letters with the digit read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand staircase is a typical feature of a large house; the question mark shows it is just one example of a part.

clue.text: Dull woman's taken over organisation, no leader

indicators.note: she has taken it over, holding the organisation within her name

parts.note: a woman's name; the 's means she has

indicators.note: without its leader the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A boring woman has taken charge of a company that lacks a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means bland and inoffensive, so dull and uninteresting.

clue.text: Re-enter MIT possibly in period as emeritus?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

explanation.surface: An old professor might go back to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology after retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeritus professor keeps an honorary title after leaving the post, during their years of being retired.

clue.text: Product indicated by the sign here!

definitions.text: Product indicated by the sign here!

parts.words: Product indicated by the sign here
parts.note: surface reading: a commercial product identified by a shop sign
setter's reading: the exclamation mark is itself the mathematical sign for a multiplicative product, as in 5! = 120

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper points to the item advertised by the sign above.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark looks like punctuation but is the sign the clue refers to: in mathematics n! means n multiplied by every whole number below it.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths a factorial is the product of all positive integers up to a number, written with an exclamation mark.

clue.text: Under way in one part of a yard

explanation.surface: Something is happening in one corner of a back garden or courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard is a measure of three feet, so one part of it is a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means in progress or happening, the same as under way.

clue.text: Person marrying after break-up may be denied second service in church

indicators.note: a break-up smashes the words apart so their letters can be reassembled
what is denied is refused, so one letter is withheld from the mix

explanation.surface: A divorcee remarrying may be refused a second wedding service in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about divorce and Church of England remarriage rules; really the letters of the first two words, minus an S, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning Prayer, or Mattins, is a daily service of the Church of England's Book of Common Prayer.

clue.text: Keeping criminal in a menial role?

explanation.surface: A prisoner held captive and put to work as a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping looks like detaining the criminal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Conserving means preserving or keeping something safe from waste or harm.

clue.text: Old poem maybe about onset of April — poet being here?

indicators.note: about here means around, so the poem's word goes round the kept letter

parts.note: a poem is an example of verses

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the month

explanation.surface: An old poem about spring, written by a poet who was abroad at the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Browning's Home-Thoughts, from Abroad, which begins 'Oh, to be in England / Now that April's there', written by a poet far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning wrote of longing for England in April while living abroad, so overseas is where the poet was.

clue.text: Enlightenment, receiving an article showing treatment centres

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the first word holds the next inside

parts.note: satori is sudden enlightenment in Zen Buddhism

explanation.surface: Spiritual insight is offered to patients at clinics.
explanation.walkthrough: The article goes at the end; only AN goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatoria, the plural of sanatorium, are institutions for treating the chronically ill or convalescent.

clue.text: Some women not completely posh are embarrassed

indicators.note: only part of the first word is used, so the answer runs on from inside it across the next words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of posh through are into the start of embarrassed

explanation.surface: A group of women who are only half genteel feel awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a variant spelling of harem, sitting across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hareem, usually spelt harem, is the women of a Muslim household, so some women.

clue.text: One very skimpy in sexual entertainment

indicators.note: in places these first pieces inside the word for sexual

parts.note: carnal means of the flesh, sexual
very cut down to almost nothing, its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A performer in a tiny costume at a racy show.
explanation.walkthrough: The skimpy costumes and samba dancers of a carnival make the surface fit the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a public festival with processions and entertainment.

clue.text: Frugal, denying a new dawn?

indicators.note: to deny is to refuse, so the word must do without the named letter

parts.note: a frugal person is sparing with money
taken as written, the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A thrifty outlook refuses to see any fresh start ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as figurative: spring is the dawn of the new year.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring is the season of renewal, figuratively the dawning of a new year after winter.

clue.text: Soldier as one often seen at the pub?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a professional soldier in the standing army

definitions.text: one often seen at the pub?

explanation.surface: A serving soldier who spends much of his time in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular names both a member of the permanent army and a habitual customer of a bar.

clue.text: Lies by fellows who get called to court?

parts.note: tales are lies, as in telling tales

explanation.surface: Falsehoods told by people who have been summoned as witnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests perjury; the definition is a rare legal word for people summoned to make up the numbers on a jury.
explanation.definitionFit: Talesmen are bystanders summoned to court to fill vacancies on a jury panel, a legal term.

clue.text: Fellow with a lot of money and a good name embraced by chum

definitions.text: Fellow with a lot of money

indicators.note: being embraced means held within arms, so these pieces sit inside the friend's word

explanation.surface: A rich man with a fine reputation is hugged by his friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a wealthy and powerful business figure, a tycoon.

clue.text: King or Queen with glitter around burial place?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shining word goes round the royal letter

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A monarch's tomb glittering with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: R serves for both Rex and Regina, so either monarch gives it. The question mark: a shrine is often, not always, a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine can be a tomb or reliquary of a saint, a holy burial place.

clue.text: Politically correct? Not the words to describe Henry VIII!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: holding the approved views

definitions.text: Not the words to describe Henry VIII!
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split into three words: correct, slender monarch, which the famously stout Tudor was not

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as RIGHT THIN KING: Henry VIII was notoriously fat, so those words do not describe him.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-thinking means holding sound, approved opinions, close to politically correct.

clue.text: Imposers of restrictions in clubs

definitions.meaning: second meaning: golf clubs with metal heads

explanation.definitionFit: Irons are both chains for prisoners, which restrict movement, and a class of golf club.

clue.text: Snare with trapped animal

indicators.note: trapped means caught inside, so the letter sits within the snare's word

explanation.surface: A trap with a creature caught in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian, a type of salamander.

clue.text: I had hesitation about learner who wouldn't make any effort

indicators.note: about means around, so the first two pieces together wrap round the beginner's letter

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An instructor dithered over a pupil who simply wouldn't try.
explanation.walkthrough: The L-plate marks a learner driver in Britain, so learner gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person, one who avoids work or exertion.

clue.text: At home old musical instrument had to be kept free from damage

parts.note: the viol is a Renaissance string instrument

explanation.surface: Someone at home had an antique instrument that needed protecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means untouched and unharmed, preserved intact.

clue.text: Material from speaker of foreign language with minimal English

parts.note: a German speaks a language foreign to English solvers

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its least part, just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Fabric bought from someone who speaks little English.
explanation.walkthrough: Material looks like cloth, but here it is the adjective meaning relevant, as in material evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or pertinent, as does material in the sense of material facts.

clue.text: Most juicy novel full of passion? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside
this flips the stated relation, so the one said to be filled does the filling instead

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel

explanation.surface: The steamiest book on the shelf is the one most packed with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the novel holds the passion; 'Quite the opposite' reverses this, so passion holds the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush means rich and succulent, so the superlative means juiciest.
